analysis.title: Coffee Break: Technology's lead is being tested, not broken
key_insights: UniCredit stays constructive on technology. It says the evidence points to broadening AI adoption rather than weakening demand, as the focus shifts from capacity build-out to monetisation.
Several recent earnings reports initially lifted sentiment, but gains faded as investors turned to capital-spending plans and financing needs.
Meta is the example cited: strong revenue growth was overshadowed by rising AI expenditure and weaker cash-flow generation.

Semiconductor and other AI-linked stocks have borne the brunt of the recent swings. The debate has moved from whether companies will spend on AI to whether the spending earns attractive returns within a reasonable timeframe.

Information technology had contributed about 7.5pp of the S&P 500's year-to-date total return by the end of last week, while making up roughly a third of the index. Health care and energy are a distant joint second at about 1.5pp each.

UniCredit expects greater performance divergence within tech. Semiconductors have the most direct exposure to infrastructure spending, with more cyclicality and higher expectations. Software and digital platforms may capture more of the next phase, though competition will decide how much of the productivity gains go to shareholders rather than customers.

Persistently high oil prices could sustain inflation and tilt the risks toward higher interest rates. Tech's longer-duration earnings leave valuations sensitive to the discount rate. A benign reassessment of the policy path would ease that constraint and act as a tailwind.

UniCredit says recent volatility has raised the burden of proof but has not broken the fundamental case. Broader sector participation would make the equity advance more resilient without needing to come at tech's expense.
Israel holds a parliamentary election today. The main blocs are Netanyahu's governing alliance and the 'change bloc' led by Gadi Eisenkot.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand for processors, memory, networking equipment and data-centre capacity remains robust. Adoption is spreading from infrastructure providers to software companies and the wider economy, and the focus is shifting from build-out to monetisation.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors question whether rising AI expenditure can generate durable revenue growth, free cash flow and attractive returns on capital. Meta's strong revenue growth was overshadowed by higher AI spending and weaker cash flow.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Not stated as a specific level or event. The report says the case holds if earnings hold up and monetisation becomes more visible.

tension_points.bull_case: A benign reassessment of the policy path would ease the valuation constraint on long-duration growth assets and provide an additional tailwind.
tension_points.bear_case: Persistently high oil prices could sustain inflationary pressure and tilt risks toward higher interest rates, which hits tech's long-duration earnings.
